title: AI military officers could be making battlefield decisions by 2030, says former CIA chief
key_facts: Retired General David Petraeus, former CIA director, told the Forecast2050 podcast that AI 'staff officers' could make battlefield decisions with little human input by 2030.
He expects 'agentic AI staff officers' within about four years, and self-governing drones in Ukraine by the end of 2026.
He said 'the side that waits for human approval before acting will lose'.
The Independent notes a 2025 Alan Turing Institute study found AI could speed commanders' decisions but not replace human judgment or accountability.
US Central Command head Admiral Brad Cooper has said humans will 'always make final decisions on what to shoot and what not to shoot, and when to shoot'.
Petraeus also said the UK could lead in autonomous warfare.
quote_evidence: “Just four years from now, we will have autonomous systems, and I think we will have the beginning of autonomous systems of autonomous systems; we will have AI agents, so you'll have agentic AI staff officers,” he told investor Finn Murphy on the Forecast2050 podcast, to be released on Thursday.
There is skepticism over whether AI could replace the traditional military chain of command.
He said human operatives will “always make final decisions on what to shoot and what not to shoot, and when to shoot”.
why_it_matters_hint: A former senior US commander predicts machines will take over staff decisions in war within years, against official statements that humans keep the final say.
notes: Full text read; comments shared exclusively with The Independent ahead of the podcast. The Admiral Cooper statement is attributed to him in the article.
